2. The short facts of this revisional application is that, Wahed Ali and Yad Ali were the original owners and possessors of the land of SA Khatian Nos. 105 and 250 and Kamaler Nessa and Ali Hossain were also the owners and possessors of the land of SA Khatian No. 250. Kamaler Nessa and Ali Hossain transferred their 14-1/2 acre of land in favour of the pre-emptor and One Rajab Ali by a registered deed dated 7-12-1959 and, as such, the pre-emptor became a co-sharer in the khatian Nos. 20 and 250 by way of purchase and also the co-sharer by way of inheritance. Smarjan, the tenant of SA Khatian No. 148, died leaving 3 sons, namely, Abul Hossain, Rajab Ali and the pre-emptor and, as such, he became co-sharer in the land of SA khatian No. 148. The pre-emptor came to know that the opposite party No.3 transferred the case land to the pre-emptee opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 by registered sale deed dated 24-8-1999 without serving any notice thereof upon the petitioner and he finally came to know of the said transfer by obtaining certified copy of the said kabala. The pre-emptee Nos. 1 and 2 are absolutely strangers in the case land and, on the other hand, the pre-emptor if the co-sharer by purchase and by inheritance in the case land and, as such, the pre-emptor is compelled to file the pre-emption petition under section 96 of the State Acquisition arid Tenancy Act upon deposit of the consideration money along with the compensation thereon in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Ishwarganj, Mymensingh being pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1999. 

 10. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and considering the documents filed by the parties. It transpires that the pre-emptor petitioner filed an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and at the time of hearing the pre-emptee opposite parties filed an interrogatory but the pre-emptor petitioner did not file any application for addition of parties. According to Exhibit No.1 and 2, it is found that there are many co-sharers in the said khatian but the petitioner has impleaded only 12 opposite parties in the pre-emption petition. Moreso, the petitioner did not file any application for addition of party in the said suit but long after three years from the filing of the appeal he filed an application for addition of party on 4-11-2003 and the appellate Court found that the said application is not sufficient to cure the petitioner's right on ground of defect of parties. Furthermore, the appellate Court opined that the pre-emptee-opposite parties are the co-sharers of the suit jotes by inheritance and also by purchase and for this reason the appellate Court rejected the amendment application and accordingly, dismissed the appeal. It further appears that PW 1 himself in his cross-examination admitted that the pre-emptee opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are the co-sharers of the suit Jote, so the pre-emption application against the co-sharers cannot be entertained.
